class.name: AIUpdateScheduler
class.brief_description: Distributes noncritical AI work across deterministic simulation tick slots.
class.description: An allocation-free per-agent scheduler inspired by periodic Behavior Tree services. Each stable integer agent ID is assigned a reproducible slot in a cycle of [member slots_per_cycle] simulation ticks. An agent is due exactly once per cycle; this spreads expensive decisions across frames without changing update order or consuming the game's random number generator. The scheduler stores no per-agent timers or lists and therefore does not require cleanup when agents despawn. Only postpone noncritical work such as periodic target rescanning or navigation repaths. Never gate physics, attacks, damage, critical perception, network reconciliation or mandatory state checks. [method is_due] supports an urgent flag that bypasses the phase gate; the caller should also preserve first-contact updates and avoid unbounded delays. Each game world should pass its authoritative monotonic tick index, not a wall clock time. This is phase staggering rather than a hard CPU-microsecond budget, a GPU scheduler, or a worker-thread pool. Use [AIExecutionProfiler] to measure the resulting work. No general optimization gain is guaranteed without profiling.

method.name: set_slots_per_cycle
method.description: Sets the cycle length from 1 to 64 slots. An invalid value is rejected without changing the previous configuration.

method.name: get_agent_slot
method.description: Returns the agent's stable hashed slot, in [code][0, slots_per_cycle)[/code]. Supports positive and negative signed 64-bit IDs.

method.name: is_due
method.description: Returns true when the agent's slot matches a nonnegative authoritative tick index. Urgent work returns true for any nonnegative tick. Negative tick indices are rejected.

method.name: ticks_until_due
method.description: Returns 0 when due now, otherwise the number of ticks before the agent's next slot, or -1 for a negative tick index.

members.member: Number of simulation-tick phases (1-64). A single slot admits every agent on every tick.
